exposure: pre-pregnancy hypertension stage I (SBP 130-139 mmHg or DBP 80-89 mmHg)
pre-pregnancy hypertension stage II (SBP >= 140 mmHg or DBP >= 90 mmHg)
pre-pregnancy elevated blood pressure (SBP 120-129 mmHg and DBP < 80 mmHg)
cohort: The study included 2038 participants from the National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health who had measured blood pressure at Wave IV (2008-09) and a singleton live birth between Waves IV and V (2016-18).
finding: Higher pre-pregnancy maternal blood pressure, including stage I and stage II hypertension, was associated with an increased risk of preterm delivery.
